learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Committed about 3% monthly-payment rise when rate goes from 4% to 7% for a $300000 thirty-year loan.
observations.exploration: At 7% payment was 1995.91, rate ratio up 75%, payment up 39%. At 10% payment 2632.71 and up 84%. Home reached 1%, payment 964.92 and down 33%; End reached 10%. Returned through 4% baseline 1432.25 to 7%.
observations.reveal: Corrected to about 39%; compared rate ratio 75% with payment 39%. Explained repeated interest on remaining debt and first-month interest 1000 versus 1750. Scoped fixed-rate thirty-year level-payment model and illustrative rates, not forecast.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 inline screenshots inspected. Payment bar with baseline marker and separate rate/payment ratio badges. Reveal readable; no principal-versus-interest decomposition shown.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner excluded history and analytics saves.
observations.blinding: No source, metadata or other judgments inspected.

prediction.reason: Clear numerical commitment targets confusion between points and payment percentage.

interaction.reason: Rate slider and baseline preset allow controlled comparisons.

payoff.reason: Reveal gives correct contrast and interest intuition but does not explain level-payment amortization.
payoff.evidence: First-month interest shown only in prose.

clarity.reason: Separate ratios and model scope reduce ambiguity.

transfer.reason: Useful fixed-model insight without a fresh borrower case.
transfer.evidence: Only rate adjustable; principal and term fixed.

accessibility.evidence: Slider endpoints worked by keyboard; other modes untested.

surprise.reason: Three percentage points imply a much larger payment change.

visualExplanation.reason: Bar displays magnitude rather than underlying repayment mechanism.

playfulness.reason: Rate exploration is responsive but plain.

practicalValue.reason: Clarifies a consequential percentage comparison within stated model.
practicalValue.evidence: Fixed principal and thirty-year level payments.

depth.evidence: No balance timeline or payment components.

complexity.reason: Familiar money quantities with two distinct percentage comparisons.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Separate percentage points, rate ratio and payment response.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Dollar values and two percentage-change badges.

whyCool: The rate ratio and payment ratio are visibly different even for the same loan.
caveat: Payment mechanism remains mostly a computed output; fixed term and principal limit transfer.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
